why1: It is two in the morning. The edit is locked, and the scene needs one more thing: the right song.
why2: So you scroll a music library for hours. Then you find the one, and wonder whether you are even allowed to use it.
why3: A wrong guess means a takedown, a demonetized video, or an awkward email to a client. The answer is buried in license text nobody reads.
why4: Needle Drop does both jobs at once. It finds the song that fits your scene, and tells you plainly whether you may use it.
intro: Here is how it works. There is one field, and everything else appears only when you need it.
describe: Describe your scene in your own words. A small language model, running on this machine, turns it into a music brief.
fast1: While it works, it searches more than twenty thousand Creative Commons tracks and checks every license. On this small computer that takes a few minutes, so we are speeding it up.
shortlist: Songs you can use stand out. The rest fade back. The asterisk means the license was checked against a 2019 snapshot, so confirm before you publish.
picks: Tap plus on any song to see why it fits, the exact license wording it relies on, and what it costs.
trace: Every run is traced with steps, tokens and spend. Running locally, the spend is zero.
use: The answer depends on your use. For a monetized video, non-commercial and no-derivatives songs are never marked cleared.
clipdrop: Or skip the words and drop in your clip. This sample has hard cuts, rain, and subtitles.
fast2: It reads the cuts, the tempo, the subtitles and a few frames, then does the same search. This is the slowest step on a small computer, so we are speeding it up.
analysis: What it saw, pacing, cuts, tempo and colors, becomes the music brief.
play: Tap a title to drop the needle, and the music plays against your clip. This sandbox can not reach Jamendo, so a stand-in track by Kevin MacLeod, licensed Creative Commons attribution, plays instead.
rate: Say whether it fits. Those ratings help check how well the system judges its own picks.
review: There is also a quick labeling screen with keyboard shortcuts.
close: That is the point. The right song for the scene, and a straight answer about whether you can use it.
github: The code, the evals, and honest notes on what is verified are on GitHub. Thanks for watching.
